newsitem.title: UK: British legislator to bring in EU referendum bill.
newsitem.headline: British legislator to bring in EU referendum bill.

text.p: British Conservative Teresa Gorman said on Monday she would introduce a bill in parliament next month calling for a referendum on Britain's membership of the European Union.

Gorman, a "Eurosceptic" opponent of further integration in the EU, said her bill aimed to give the people of Britain the option of pulling out of the bloc. She said she had won a slot on January 21 for introducing the proposal.
"People on both sides of the political fence are frustrated because they are not being asked for their opinion. A referendum is essential to clear the air," Gorman said.

Gorman's bill was announced just a day after Prime Minister John Major appealed for unity his Conservative Party in the run-up to the next general election, which he plans to call no later than next May 1.

Major, whose one-seat parliamnetary majority vanished when a disaffected Conservative MP withdrew support last week over a hospital casualty department closure, said on Sunday he would not be held to ransom by "maverick" Eurosceptics intent on making trouble.
Gorman will introduce the bill under the so-called 10-minute rule which gives members of parliament an opportunity to discuss matters of importance. But the bill has almost no chance of becoming law.

Gorman said she had the support of other Eurosceptics who were thrown out of the Conservative parliamentary party in November 1994 for rebelling against government policy on links with the European Union.
